title: Income Tax Provision: What ASC 740 Requires Before Your Audit
summary: The ASC 740 income tax provision pairs current tax with deferred taxes. See how private companies build it and when a valuation allowance applies.
body_markdown:
## What Is an Income Tax Provision?


An ASC 740 income tax provision is total income tax expense for the period, equal to current tax expense or benefit plus deferred tax expense or benefit. It is not the tax return, and it will rarely equal cash taxes paid. ASC 740 exists so the income statement carries the tax consequences of events in the period those events are recognized for book purposes, rather than in the period the tax law happens to tax them.


Three framings matter if you’re heading into a first audit.


- **It’s a PBC deliverable with its own timeline.** The provision, the deferred tax rollforward, the valuation allowance memo, and the income tax footnote are four separate work products, and they arrive on the[audit prep checklist](https://www.indinero.com/blog/audit-prep-for-startups-checklist/) as four separate requests. Closing in five days and then spending six weeks on the provision hasn’t shortened your audit.
- **It covers more than federal income tax.** ASC 740-10-15-3 pulls domestic federal, foreign, and state and local taxes based on income into scope, including franchise taxes measured by income.
- **Permanent and temporary differences do different jobs.** A permanent difference changes total tax expense. A temporary difference only moves it between current and deferred. That’s the whole distinction, and it’s the last you need before the computation.


The income tax provision for private companies runs on the same recognition and measurement model that applies to registrants. The relief sits in the disclosure, and it’s paragraph-specific rather than general. Everything below the recognition line still has to happen, including the gross deferred inventory, the realizability analysis, and the reconciliation between the statutory and effective rates.


## The ASC 740 Computation


The ASC 740 computation runs in a fixed order, and the order is what keeps the rate reconciliation from turning into a plug.


1. **Current tax.** Bridge book income to taxable income by jurisdiction, then compute the tax payable or refundable on each return.
2. **Deferred inventory.** Build the book versus tax balance sheet and tax-effect every temporary difference at the enacted rate expected to apply on reversal.
3. **Realizability.** Test the resulting deferred tax assets and record a valuation allowance where the more-likely-than-not threshold isn’t met.
4. **Rollforward.** Prove the change in net deferred balances against the deferred piece of the income statement.
5. **Disclosure.** Assemble the footnote, including the components of expense and the valuation allowance activity.


A change in tax law lands in the **period of enactment** , not on the effective date, under ASC 740-10-35-4. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act was signed July 4, 2025, so calendar-year companies remeasured deferred balances in the third quarter of 2025 regardless of when the underlying rules began to apply.


Presentation has its own constraint. Under ASC 740-10-45-6, deferred tax assets and liabilities offset only within the same tax-paying component and the same tax jurisdiction. A federal deferred tax liability can’t be netted against a state deferred tax asset, and a US deferred tax asset can’t be netted against a foreign one. All deferred balances sit noncurrent on a classified balance sheet.


None of it works on a trial balance that’s still moving. The provision inherits whatever discipline your[month-end close](https://www.indinero.com/blog/month-end-close-checklist-saas/) already has.


### Current Tax Versus Deferred Tax


Current tax expense is the tax payable or refundable on the current-year return. Deferred tax expense or benefit is the period change in the net deferred tax asset or liability balance. Current and deferred tax expense added together is the total provision.


The rate mechanics are where private companies go wrong. ASC 740-10-30-8 measures deferred balances at the **enacted** rate expected to apply when the temporary difference affects taxes payable or refundable, which is not always the period of reversal and is almost never the current-year rate. The federal corporate rate is 21 percent. The state layer gets built separately, net of the federal benefit of the state deduction. The AICPA’s worked example runs a 6 percent state rate down to a 19.74 percent federal deferred rate, 21 percent less 1.26 percent, for a combined deferred rate of 25.74 percent.


Two refinements follow. The state rate has to reflect the apportionment factors expected to apply in future years, not current-year apportionment. And ASC 740 requires deferred taxes to be determined separately for each entity and each taxing jurisdiction.


One blended state rate ages fast.


### Building the Deferred Tax Inventory


The deferred tax inventory a growth-stage SaaS or mid-market company actually carries is shorter than the textbook list and far more specific.


**Deferred tax assets**


- **Net operating loss carryforwards.** Post-2017 NOLs carry forward indefinitely but offset only 80 percent of taxable income in years beginning after 2020, under IRC Section 172(a)(2). The cap means the asset reverses more slowly than a straight-line model assumes.
- **Deferred revenue.** Usually the largest single temporary difference on a SaaS balance sheet, and usually a short one. Section 451(b) puts the all-events test no later than inclusion in the applicable financial statement, and the Section 451(c) deferral method under Treas. Reg. 1.451-8 picks up the remainder in the next taxable year.
- **Accrued compensation and bonuses** not paid inside the window the deduction timing rules allow.
- **Capitalized research and experimental expenditures,** federal only, and only the residual 2022 through 2024 balance.
- **Stock compensation on NQSOs.** Cumulative ASC 718 book expense on unexercised nonqualified options.
- **ASC 842 lease liability,** recognized for book and absent from the tax balance sheet.
- **Allowance for credit losses** under ASC 326. Book reserve now, tax deduction on worthlessness.


**Deferred tax liabilities**


- **ASC 842 right-of-use asset.** The asset and the liability are initially measured the same way, so on a plain operating lease the two differences start at nearly the same amount and move close to in step. They’re still two differences, and both belong in the schedule.
- **Capitalized commissions.** Amortized over the period of benefit for book under[ASC 340-40 commission capitalization](https://www.indinero.com/blog/sales-commission-capitalization-asc-340-40/) , generally deducted when paid for tax.
- **Depreciation.** The One Big Beautiful Bill Act permanently restored 100 percent bonus depreciation under Section 168(k) for qualifying property acquired and placed in service after January 19, 2025, which widens the book versus tax gap again.


New IRC Section 174A allows a current deduction for domestic research or experimental expenditures paid or incurred in tax years beginning after December 31, 2024, with an election under Section 174A(c)(1) to capitalize and amortize over not less than 60 months. Section 174A(d)(3) treats software development costs as research or experimental, and foreign research stays on 15-year amortization under Section 174.[Rev. Proc. 2025-28](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-28.pdf) lets affected taxpayers deduct unamortized 2022 through 2024 amounts over a one-year or two-year period beginning in 2025, and lets taxpayers with three-year average gross receipts of $31 million or less amend 2022 through 2024 returns instead. So the federal Section 174 deferred tax asset unwinds, and the speed depends on which transition election you made.


California is the part most explainers get wrong. SB 711, signed October 1, 2025, moved California’s general IRC conformity date to January 1, 2025, so it doesn’t reach the One Big Beautiful Bill Act at all. California also still applies IRC Section 174 as it read on January 1, 2015, which means research and experimental costs have been currently deductible for California the whole time. The provision consequence is clean. That 2022 through 2024 Section 174 deferred tax asset was federal-only, and the federal unwind has no California counterpart to model.


### The More-Likely-Than-Not Valuation Allowance Test


A deferred tax asset valuation allowance reduces the asset unless realization is more likely than not, which ASC 740-10-30-5(e) sets above 50 percent on the weight of all available evidence. In strict terms 50.0 percent requires an allowance and 50.1 percent does not, which is why this is a documented memo rather than a calculation.


ASC 740-10-30-18 lists four sources of future taxable income available to realize the asset: reversals of existing taxable temporary differences, future taxable income exclusive of reversing differences and carryforwards, taxable income in prior carryback years where carryback is permitted, and tax-planning strategies that would be implemented if necessary. They’re weighted by objectivity. Forecasts are the weakest of the four.


A cumulative loss in recent years is the evidence that decides it, measured in practice as aggregate pretax book earnings for the current year plus the two preceding years, adjusted for permanent differences. ASC 740-10-30-21 treats that as objectively verifiable negative evidence, and ASC 740-10-30-23 weights recent operating results above projections, so a forecast rarely overcomes it.


Here’s the outcome nobody states plainly. A venture-backed company that has lost money for three straight years will carry a **full** valuation allowance. The net deferred tax asset on the balance sheet is zero, and the reported provision collapses to state minimum and gross-receipts-style income taxes plus any foreign tax on an offshore subsidiary.


A calendar 2026 example. Pretax book loss of $8.0 million, three-year cumulative pretax result of negative $21.3 million, combined deferred rate of 25.74 percent.


Deferred item Gross difference Tax effect at 25.74%


Federal and state NOL carryforwards $22,000,000 $5,662,800 DTA


Deferred revenue, net of 451(c) acceleration $1,200,000 $308,880 DTA


Accrued compensation $600,000 $154,440 DTA


NQSO stock compensation $3,000,000 $772,200 DTA


ASC 842 lease liability $2,400,000 $617,760 DTA


Allowance for credit losses $250,000 $64,350 DTA


ASC 842 right-of-use asset $(2,250,000) $(579,150) DTL


ASC 340-40 capitalized commissions $(1,800,000) $(463,320) DTL


Depreciation $(900,000) $(231,660) DTL


**Net deferred tax asset before allowance** **$6,306,300**


Valuation allowance $(6,306,300)


**Net deferred tax asset reported** **$0**


Current tax is zero federal plus roughly $12,000 of state taxes inside ASC 740 scope, including California’s $800 minimum franchise tax. That’s a total provision near $12,000 on an $8.0 million pretax loss, an effective rate around negative 0.15 percent.


The deferred lines are not blank in the rollforward. A gross deferred benefit of, say, $1.9 million is offset by a $1.9 million valuation allowance charge, and both appear as significant components of income tax expense under ASC 740-10-50-9. A provision showing zero deferred activity in a loss year has almost certainly skipped the gross calculation.


Zero balance, not zero work.


Release runs the same test in reverse, and the positive evidence auditors credit is cumulative three-year pretax income in the jurisdiction plus a forecast management has a record of hitting. ASC 740 never defines “recent years,” so timing is a judgment call, which is why auditors test the controls over management’s evaluation and assess its historical forecasting accuracy. Release lands as a large one-time benefit and can drive a negative effective rate in the year it happens.


## SaaS-Specific Application


SaaS balance sheets concentrate the ASC 740 work in four places, and deferred revenue is both the largest and the most frequently overstated.


- **Deferred revenue is short.** Section 451(b) accelerates recognition to the applicable financial statement date and Section 451(c) permits only a one-year deferral of the remainder, so a $4 million book deferred revenue balance may support well under $1.5 million of temporary difference. Tax-effect the full book balance and the asset is wrong before the allowance analysis even starts. The[ASC 606 recognition pattern](https://www.indinero.com/blog/asc-606-what-you-need-to-know/) that built the balance is what dictates the gap.
- **ISOs and NQSOs split.** An incentive stock option generates ASC 718 book expense and, absent a disqualifying disposition, no corporate deduction, so it’s a permanent difference with no deferred tax asset. A nonqualified option is temporary. Under ASC 718-740-35-2 the excess tax benefit or deficiency at exercise runs through current income tax expense in the period it arises rather than to APIC, and a full valuation allowance absorbs the windfall.
- **Section 382 changes the asset you’re testing.** An ownership change limits annual use of pre-change NOLs to the value of the old loss corporation multiplied by the long-term tax-exempt rate, and a priced round can trigger it. The provision consequence is narrow. A limited NOL may be unrealizable within its carryforward life, which is a realizability problem in its own right.
- **Offshore development subsidiaries** bring transfer pricing exposure, intercompany service charges, and a foreign current tax number that survives a US full valuation allowance. That foreign tax is often the only real number in a loss-making group’s provision, which is why[SaaS accounting](https://www.indinero.com/industries/saas-accounting-services/) and tax work stop being separable once a second entity exists.


## Common Pitfalls


Seven errors account for most of the audit comments growth-stage companies get on the provision.


1. **Measuring deferreds at the current-year rate** instead of the enacted rate expected to apply when the difference affects taxes payable or refundable. This is the most common private-company error.
2. **Omitting the state deferred rate entirely,** or applying one blended rate across a dozen filing jurisdictions with different apportionment factors.
3. **Netting across jurisdictions that can’t be netted** under ASC 740-10-45-6, usually a federal liability against a state asset.
4. **Concluding that a full valuation allowance means no provision work.** The gross inventory, the allowance memo, the rate reconciliation, and the full disclosure set are all still required, and all of them are[audit preparation](https://www.indinero.com/blog/audit-preparation/) items with due dates.
5. **Missing the ASC 842 pair.** The right-of-use asset and the lease liability are two temporary differences, not one net amount.
6. **Putting Delaware franchise tax in the provision.** Delaware computes its corporate franchise tax under the authorized shares method or the assumed par value capital method, with a $175 minimum under the first, a $400 minimum under the second, and a $200,000 cap. It isn’t measured by income, and ASC 740-10-15-4(a) scopes out a franchise tax to the extent it’s based on capital or another non-income amount. California is the opposite case. The FTB’s[Publication 1060](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/misc/1060.html) puts the state’s corporate franchise tax at 8.84 percent of California net income with an $800 minimum, which makes it a tax based on income and places it inside the provision.
7. **Treating a law change as effective-date news.** The One Big Beautiful Bill Act’s provision effects belonged to the quarter containing July 4, 2025, not to the first period its rules applied.


## The Audit-Ready Standard


ASC 740 disclosure requirements split on public business entity status, and the private-company relief is paragraph-specific rather than general.


- **ASC 740-10-50-9.** Significant components of income tax expense from continuing operations, including current expense, deferred expense, and adjustments for enacted changes in tax law or rates. All entities.
- **ASC 740-10-50-2.** Total deferred tax liabilities, total deferred tax assets, total valuation allowance, and the net change in the allowance for the period.
- **ASC 740-10-50-6 and 50-8.** Public business entities disclose the approximate tax effect of each type of significant temporary difference and carryforward. A non-PBE discloses the types qualitatively, with no quantitative effect by type.
- **ASC 740-10-50-12, 50-12A and 50-13.** The numerical rate reconciliation in dollars and percentages is PBE-only. A non-PBE qualitatively discloses the nature and effect of the specific reconciling categories and the individual jurisdictions driving a significant difference between the statutory and effective rates.
- **ASC 740-10-50-15A.** The tabular rollforward of unrecognized tax benefits is PBE-only. Non-PBEs stay subject to the rest of 740-10-50-15.


[ASU 2023-09](https://storage.fasb.org/ASU%202023-09.pdf) is the 2026 hook, and it does reach private companies. It’s effective for public business entities for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2024, and for all other entities for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2025, which is fiscal 2026 for a calendar-year private company. The eight-category rate reconciliation table and the 5 percent disaggregation threshold apply only to PBEs. The income-taxes-paid disclosure applies to all entities: income taxes paid net of refunds received, disaggregated by federal, state and local, and foreign, with further breakout by individual jurisdiction at 5 percent or more of the total. Most private companies have never tracked cash taxes that way.


Uncertain tax positions are two steps, and the citation is two paragraphs. Recognize under ASC 740-10-25-6 only if the position is more likely than not to be sustained on its technical merits, assuming examination by a taxing authority with full knowledge of the facts. Then measure under ASC 740-10-30-7 at the largest amount of benefit that is cumulatively more likely than not to be realized on settlement. At a private company the triggers are state nonfiling and nexus positions, aggressive research credit claims, and transfer pricing with an offshore entity. On nexus the AICPA’s analysis is direct. A taxpayer asserting no filing obligation has to clear the threshold on technical merits alone, and if it can’t, it records the entire position including interest and penalties.


Interim reporting adds a forecast dependency. ASC 740-270 requires an estimated annual effective tax rate applied to year-to-date ordinary income or loss, with significant unusual or infrequent items and items whose effect can’t be estimated computed discretely under ASC 740-270-25-3.


Auditor independence is where a blanket claim goes wrong, and the split matters in front of your audit committee.


- **Issuers.** SEC Regulation S-X Rule 2-01(c)(4)(i) prohibits bookkeeping services for an audit client, on the principle that a firm can’t audit its own work, and the rulemaking behind it sits in[Release 33-8183](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/final/33-8183.htm) . Tax services need audit committee pre-approval, and[PCAOB Rule 3524](https://pcaobus.org/news-events/news-releases/news-release-detail/sec-approves-pcaob-rules-on-auditor-ethics-independence-and-tax-services_174) requires the firm to describe the proposed services in writing, discuss the independence implications, and document that discussion.
- **Private companies.** AICPA rules govern and the provision is a nonattest service. The client takes responsibility, designates a competent individual to oversee the work, and has to have the skill, knowledge, and experience to evaluate it. The firm then evaluates self-review and management-participation threats. Many audit firms decline anyway, because the provision is a material estimate they would turn around and audit. The revised Tax Services interpretation, ET section 1.295.160, takes effect January 15, 2027, with early implementation permitted.


That’s the honest reason the provision sits with you or with an outsourced accounting and[business tax](https://www.indinero.com/services/business-tax-services/) team like indinero’s, and not with the firm signing the opinion.

## Frequently asked questions


The questions Controllers and finance leads ask most often about the ASC 740 income tax provision, answered below.


### Does a company with no taxable income still need a tax provision?


Yes, a loss year still requires a full ASC 740 provision, because deferred balances move and the valuation allowance conclusion has to be documented. In practice the number often collapses to state minimum and gross-receipts-style income taxes plus any foreign tax on an offshore subsidiary. The gross deferred inventory, the allowance memo, and the footnote are still required, and a provision showing zero deferred activity in a loss year has almost certainly skipped the gross calculation.


### Can our auditor prepare the provision they then audit?


SEC Regulation S-X prohibits your auditor from preparing the provision at an issuer, while at a private company it’s a nonattest service requiring safeguards. Under AICPA rules the client assumes management responsibility, designates a competent individual to oversee the work, and the firm evaluates self-review and management-participation threats. Many audit firms decline regardless, because the provision is a material estimate they would turn around and audit, which is why the work sits with you or an outsourced accounting and tax team.


### What does an income tax provision cost to prepare?


There’s no published market rate for ASC 740 provision preparation, so cost depends on jurisdiction count, entity structure, and deferred inventory complexity. The drivers are countable: the number of state filing jurisdictions and whether apportionment data exists, the number of legal entities, whether a foreign subsidiary is involved, whether the allowance memo is a first-year build or a rollforward, and whether you need an annual provision or quarterly ones under ASC 740-270. A free consultation with indinero’s business tax team scopes the deliverable for your situation.


### Can we release the valuation allowance the year we turn profitable?


Releasing a valuation allowance after one profitable year is rarely supportable, because a cumulative three-year loss is objectively verifiable negative evidence under ASC 740-10-30-21. Release generally needs cumulative three-year pretax income in the jurisdiction plus forecasts management has a record of hitting, since ASC 740-10-30-23 weights recent operating results above projections. The release lands as a large one-time benefit and can drive a negative effective rate, so auditors test the controls over management’s evaluation and its historical forecasting accuracy.


### Does registering in more states change the provision?


Yes, new state registrations change current state tax, add state deferred rates, and shift the apportionment factors your deferred balances are measured at. ASC 740-10-30-8 measures deferreds at the enacted rate expected to apply on reversal, so the state layer has to reflect future apportionment rather than this year’s. Registration also touches the uncertain tax position analysis, since a prior assertion of no filing obligation has to clear the more-likely-than-not threshold on technical merits alone under ASC 740-10-25-6.
